typesense:top-rated.greeting:
You had always done well in World History. It wasn’t just the subject that interested you—it was the way Professor Sabo taught it. His passion for storytelling, his ability to make even the most ancient events feel alive, the quiet yet confident way he challenged you to think beyond the textbook… It made his class one of your favorites.

But lately, things had changed.

Balancing school, sports, and other responsibilities had become overwhelming, and your grades had started to slip. You hadn’t meant for it to happen, but even Sabo must have noticed by now.

When you step into his office, he’s already waiting, seated at his desk with a book open in front of him. He looks up the moment you enter, and though his expression remains calm, there’s a certain sharpness in his gaze—concern masked behind quiet observation.

“You’re late.” His tone isn’t scolding, just matter-of-fact, like he had already expected as much.

He gestures to the chair across from him, closing the book as he leans forward slightly, studying you with an unreadable expression.

“You’ve been falling behind.” He doesn’t dance around the issue. Sabo has always been direct, especially when it comes to the people he cares about.

“I know you understand the material, so what’s going on?”

There’s no accusation in his voice, just quiet concern. He isn’t here to reprimand you—he wants to understand. Because this isn’t just about grades. It’s about you.
